params.body:
Two places read an absence as a confirmation.

**A dealer who never opened the pane had accepted nothing (finding `de-module-is-pas-actief-als-alle`, #581, R P2-7.1).** `RealGarantService::isEnabled` compared how many consent settings were stored with how many were accepted. A dealer who never opened that pane has no rows at all, and nought equals nought, so he counted as having accepted. What actually held him back were the credentials, not his consent. It now counts how many of the four stand at `1` and asks for four; the list lives once, as `RealGarantService::CONSENTS`, instead of being written out twice inside the same method.

**A 500 is not an arrival (finding `een-bericht-dat-niet-aankomt-wordt-drie`, #586, R S2-10.11).** The rule promises three attempts. It turned out worse than the finding said: not even a connection error was ever retried. `deliver` caught every error itself and returned nothing, so the job always ended successfully and `$tries = 3` was never once used — a partner answering 500 for a week looked exactly like a partner processing everything.

`deliver` now says whether the message arrived. A 4xx or 5xx is not an arrival: the answer and the reason land in `webhook_deliveries` (`error` = `HTTP 500`), which is what turns the row red on the pane, and a delivery that failed does not count as received — so the change-detection of R S2-10.12 lets the next identical message go out instead of holding it back.

`SendVehicleWebhookJob` hands the job back to the queue when the answer is no. **Releasing, not throwing, on purpose:** outside production the queue is forced to `sync` by `Outbound::seal()`, and a throw would land in the dealer's save — a partner answering 500 must not break a vehicle sheet. Releasing does nothing on `sync` (there is no one to pick it up) and on a real queue does exactly what the rule promises: again, up to three times, then no more and without a notification. The direct path (not through the queue) stays silent as it always was.

`SilenceIsNotAYesTest` covers both: no rows, three of four and four of four for the consents; 500, 200, and a 503 followed by a 200 for the webhook; and a queued job that goes back on the queue when the message did not arrive and stays off it when it did. Both were checked against the unfixed code.

One aside worth recording: halfway through this branch `RealGarantServiceTest` failed because a RealGarant token from an earlier test run was still in `storage/framework/cache`. That is finding #604 (`CACHE_STORE` versus `CACHE_DRIVER`) reproducing itself; it is fixed in #691.

Fixes bevinding de-module-is-pas-actief-als-alle, bevinding een-bericht-dat-niet-aankomt-wordt-drie.
Fixes #581
Fixes #586

params.title: A silence is not a yes
